title: Office of Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Launches the “S&T Cluster Annual Report 2025-2026”
body_text:
The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India launched the “Science and Technology (S&T) Clusters Annual Report 2025–26” under the chairmanship of Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser during a meeting held on 13 August 2026. The launch was also attended by Dr (Mrs) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary; Dr Vishal Choudhary, Scientist-F; Dr Santhosh Nair, Scientist-D; and Dr Shefali Uttam, Technical Staff, Office of the PSA, along with the CEOs, COOs, and Principal Investigators of the eight S&T Clusters established under the Office of the PSA: Andhra Pradesh Medtech Zone (AMTZ Vizag); Bengaluru Science and Technology Cluster (BeST); Bhubaneswar City Knowledge and Innovation Cluster (BCKIC); Delhi Research Implementation and Innovation Cluster (DRIIV); Jodhpur City Knowledge and Innovation Cluster (JCKIC); Panjab University–IIT Ropar Regional Accelerator for Holistic Innovations (PI-RAHI); Pune Knowledge Cluster (PKC); and Research and Innovation Circle of Hyderabad (RICH).
During the launch, Prof. Sood emphasised stronger inter-cluster collaboration, industry engagement, and technology translation, with a focus on adapting and scaling successful regional solutions and measuring outcomes through higher TRLs, real-world validation, commercialisation, and societal and economic impact.
Dr Maini highlighted the growing maturity of the S&T Clusters through a consortium-based model and emphasised the need to prioritise the national interest while strengthening industry participation in technology validation and translation.
The Report highlights the evolving role of S&T Clusters as regional innovation ecosystems and “National Technology Accelerators”, driving technology translation through shared infrastructure, public-private partnerships, startup support, and industry engagement. Several initiatives have progressed from research and pilot validation to field deployment and commercialisation, including E-Yantram, AI-enabled Digital Podiatry Clinics, AI-enabled agriculture and weather intelligence, indigenous pacemaker components, patient-specific 3D-printed implants, ChemAmaze, and One Health initiatives, alongside national platforms such as Kalaanubhav.in and i-Passport. The Report also mentions the growing international engagement of the Clusters, including the First International Conference on S&T Clusters held in December 2025, which brought together participants from over 35 countries and resulted in 12 international MoUs, followed by collaborations with the University of Western Australia, the India-Australia Smart Farm Network and the UK Catapult Network in areas including health, emerging technologies and net-zero technologies.
The S&T Clusters also presented their international collaborations that are underway across areas such as healthcare, advanced manufacturing, smart agriculture, sustainable mobility, climate resilience, emerging technologies and capacity building. Inter-Cluster collaborations has enabled successful solutions to be replicated and scaled. The Digital Podiatry Clinic, for instance, has expanded from BeST to PI-RAHI, Kalaanubhav.in , an initiative of JCKIC, is being scaled across Clusters, and I-RISE, a program of I-STEM is strengthening access to advanced scientific infrastructure through the S&T Clusters. The i-Passport initiative of AMTZ is also being considered for national scale-up, providing innovators with access to shared infrastructure, testing, mentorship, regulatory support and industry networks.
The Report can be accessed through: https://www.psa.gov.in/CMS/web/sites/default/files/2026-08/S%26T%20Clusters%20Annual%20Report%202025-26.pdf

ministry.name: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI

enrichment.summary: The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India launched the 'S&T Clusters Annual Report 2025-26' on 13 August 2026 under Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, showcasing progress by eight S&T Clusters across India. The report highlights technology translation successes like AI-enabled Digital Podiatry Clinics, indigenous pacemaker components, 3D-printed implants, and platforms like Kalaanubhav.in and i-Passport, alongside growing international collaborations including 12 MoUs from a December 2025 international conference attended by 35+ countries.
enrichment.context:
The S&T Cluster initiative was launched by the Office of the PSA to create regional innovation ecosystems that bridge the gap between research institutions, industry, and government to accelerate technology translation and commercialization in India. These eight clusters (spanning cities like Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar, Jodhpur, Delhi, and a Punjab-IIT Ropar collaboration, plus the specialized AMTZ Vizag medtech zone) function as consortium-based hubs pooling academic, industrial, and government resources to move innovations from lab-scale research to field deployment, addressing India's historical challenge of weak industry-academia linkages and low commercialization rates of publicly funded research. The Office of the PSA itself was constituted to provide high-level scientific advice to the Prime Minister and coordinate India's science, technology, and innovation ecosystem across ministries.

This annual report reflects India's broader push to strengthen its innovation and manufacturing base under initiatives like Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, particularly in strategic sectors like medical technology (reducing import dependence on devices like pacemakers and implants), agriculture (AI-enabled climate and farm intelligence), and health tech. The growing international engagement—MoUs with Australia and the UK—signals India's attempt to integrate its innovation clusters into global R&D networks, particularly in areas like net-zero technologies and smart agriculture, which are priority areas for international scientific diplomacy and technology transfer.
